 respondent/State.

Order 
This is repeat (fourth) application filed on behalf of applicant under Section 483 of BNSS for grant of bail relating to Crime No.148 of 2021 registered by Police Station - Malajkhand District- Balaghat (M.P.) for commission of offence under Sections 307, 326, 498A and 302 of IPC.
Applicant is in custody since 25.07.2021.

His second bail application was dismissed as withdrawn with liberty to renew the prayer once the person who recorded the dying declaration of the deceased, is examined in the Court of law on 09.08.2024.
2.

Prosecution story in brief is that on 24.07.2021, the police received information that Bhagrati Satyam of Gram Pauni had been set on fire by her husband, Purshottam Satyam, and was admitted to CHC Birsa for treatment.

She stated that her husband, a habitual drinker, poured kerosene over her and NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-JBP:636 2 MCRC-46490-2025 set her on fire after accusing her of an illicit relationship and threatening to take another wife.
She suffered burns over approximately 90% of her body.
At the time, no one else was present.

In the evening, her aunt,
Hemlata Warkade, contacted her brother Manoj Uikey and took her to the hospital, where she recorded her statement to the police.

Accordingly, Crime No. 148/2021 under Sections 307, 306,
and 498-A of the IPC was registered.
3. Learned counsel for applicant has submitted that applicant is innocent and has been falsely implicated in the case.
Deceased was not properly treated.
She was admitted to the Hospital at 1:40 a.m. and discharged at 2:00 a,m,.
It is further submitted that she was kept at home and was not provided proper treatment, therefore, her life could not be saved.
In this regard, learned counsel for the applicant has drawn attention of this Court to the statement of Dr. Bisen (PW-10).

sentences.text: Therefore, it has been prayed that applicant/accused be enlarged on bail.
4. Learned Deputy Government Advocate for the respondent/State, on the other hand has opposed the bail application but fairly submits that applicant has no criminal antecedents.
5. Considering the period of custody and all the facts and circumstances of the case, but without commenting on merit of the case, I am inclined to release the applicant on bail.
Consequently, bail application under Section 483 of BNSS for grant of bail filed on behalf of applicant, stands allowed.

6. It is directed that applicant be released on bail on his furnishing a NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2026:MPHC-JBP:636 3 MCRC-46490-2025 personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand only) with one solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court, for his regular appearance before the trial Court during trial with a condition that he shall remain present before the concerned Court on all the dates fixed by it during trial.

He shall abide by all the conditions enumerated under Section 480(3) of BNSS.
7.
This order shall be effective till the end of the trial.
However, in case of bail jump and breach of any of the conditions of bail, it shall become ineffective.
Certified copy as per rules.
